specificTasks: (1) Background Research - reviewed literature on PETase and MHETase enzymes, including FAST-PETase, to assess degradation of polyester microfibres captured from laundry wastewater, covering enzyme stability, reaction conditions, and limits of integration into filtration systems; (2) Analysis - evaluated the feasibility of combining laundry microfibre filtration with enzymatic PET degradation, including filter-integrated treatment, and identified technical challenges that need validation; (3) Entrepreneurship - conducted market research, competitor analysis, and commercialization assessments covering microfibre filtration technologies, potential partners, market barriers, and regulation; (4) Public Engagement - identified potential customers and collaborators, including filtration companies and appliance manufacturers, and prepared outreach templates and customer discovery questions; (5) Writing - prepared research summaries, feasibility assessments, competitor comparisons, and commercialization materials.

specificTasks: (1) Analysis - embedded ~60,000 PETadex enzymes and projected them to 2D with UMAP for the PETadex Atlas on petadex.net; (2) Software - wrote the embedding and UMAP workflow for the Atlas and automated conversion of dry lab notebooks to wiki-ready Markdown with GitHub Actions; (3) Notebook/record keeping - ported all dry lab experiment records to the wiki through the automated notebook pipeline; (4) Wiki Coding - led integration of all dry lab members' work and notebooks into the wiki; (5) Visualization - built the PETadex Atlas data visualization and the dry lab poster presented at the UofT Microplastics Conference; (6) Writing - contributed to the PETadex manuscript.

specificTasks: (1) Investigation - performed wet lab experiments and collected experimental data; (2) Notebook/record keeping - recorded lab activities during shifts; (3) Writing - co-wrote the safety section of the wet lab wiki; (4) Background Research - reviewed published articles for the data scraping project; (5) Data Curation - scraped and compiled data from published articles for the data scraping project paper.

name: Sara Habibi
specificTasks: (1) Conceptualization - as Wet Lab Selection Subteam Lead, helped develop and refine the selection assay linking PETase activity to bacterial survival through antibiotic resistance; (2) Background Research - researched antibiotic resistance markers (sul1, sul2, dfrB10), including mechanisms, growth media, and limitations, as well as copper toxicity, the pCusC promoter, background resistance, and promoter leakiness; (3) Investigation - helped plan the selection assay approach, including antibiotic selection, copper induction, controls, and sources of false positives and false negatives; (4) Analysis - compared sul1, sul2, and dfrB10 performance and helped decide which approaches to pursue; (5) Project Administration - led and coordinated the Selection Subteam's research, experimental planning, and decisions; (6) Writing - wrote the selection assay section of the wiki, covering background, design rationale, methods, troubleshooting, limitations, and future directions.

name: Sara Parvaresh Rizi
specificTasks: (1) Analysis - analyzed CATH and InterPro domain data to build per-family profile pages with domain-architecture comparisons, implemented patristic-distance and k-nearest-neighbour filtering in the phylogenetic tree viewer, and mapped per-residue features from the SQL database onto ORF IDs; (2) Background Research - researched and documented the team's niche CATH domains against InterPro, RCSB PDB, and EBI HMM profiles, and evaluated visualization libraries (Nightingale, feature-viewer, Skylign) before selecting the final approach; (3) Notebook/record keeping - built the hardware notebook page and the Contributions calendar and kept both current from meeting minutes; (4) Project Administration - coordinated the CATH contribution pages, standardized layout conventions across non-homepage pages, integrated other members' frontend work (90% cluster search, search hub and SRA data, SignalP, paper tree), and helped delegate tasks in web and wiki meetings; (5) Wiki Coding - built the wiki homepage (parallax illustration, animations, scroll sequence, mobile layout, new logo), the Meet the Team page, the Hardware parts page with an interactive system-architecture diagram, the Outreach flip-book page, phylogenetic tree search, and cross-page navigation for CATH domains; (6) Visualization - built the 2D protein feature visualizer with a pLDDT track, the InterPro domain-architecture viewer, and interactive HMM logos for each CATH page, and rebuilt the hardware system architecture as interactive JavaScript.

name: Shivangi Roy
